messages:
emma: heads up — mypy is spamming in the sample-app CI. failing checks are around the autogenerated pydantic models for responses. lots of `List[Foo] | None` vs `Optional[List[Foo]]` noise and a couple of `Any` holes

kai: ugh. is this the generator outputting `Union[List[Foo], None]` or is it from `typing_extensions` weirdness? can you paste one of the offending signatures? :eyes:

emma: here's a trimmed snippet from the client method return type the generator made:
```python
def list_items() -> Generator[dict, None, None]:
    ...
```
and the model file has `items: list[Item] | None` which mypy flags when we use `from __future__ import annotations` in the app. pyright also complains about mixed builtin/list vs typing.List in other places.

jun: two separate issues imo: (1) the generator isn't emitting typing stubs, so consumers get runtime models (pydantic BaseModel subclasses) typed as `Any` in some call-sites, and (2) the union/Optional formatting — py3.10+ supports `list[Foo] | None` but some typecheckers config require `from __future__ import annotations` or `typing_extensions`.

maria: we've been debating whether to ship a tiny stub package `redwood-sdk-types` that only exposes types for generated models. that would let us keep runtime pydantic models but give proper static types to consumers.

kai: stub package sounds right. alternative is to make the generator emit `.pyi` next to each module. stubgen could do that but keeping it in our toolchain might be cleaner. also streaming APIs need typed async iterators — currently we return `AsyncGenerator[bytes, None]` at runtime, which yields raw chunks. for users who wrap those chunks into `str`/`Model`, they want a typed `AsyncIterator[Model]` option.

emma: ex of streaming method signature I've seen from the SDK: `async def stream_chat(...) -> AsyncIterator[Union[str, dict]]:` which ends up unreadable. i'd prefer a typed wrapper: `AsyncIterator[ChatDelta]` where ChatDelta is the union-like pydantic model we already generate.

jun: small implementation proposal: generator emits a `types.pyi` module that declares all top-level model types using `TypedDict` / class stubs for pydantic models. CLI flag `--emit-pyi`. Then we publish those pyi files into the wheel so pip installs have proper typing for both mypy and pyright. this avoids a separate package.

maria: watchout for forward refs and `from __future__ import annotations` — we must ensure the pyi representation resolves names the same way. testing locally, mypy still complains when models reference each other in lists: `List["Foo"]` vs `list[Foo]` mismatch. maybe normalise to `from typing import List, Optional` in the pyi content.

kai: agreed. make pyi target py3.8+ using typing.List/Optional is safest. and include `if TYPE_CHECKING: from .models import Foo` patterns if needed.

emma: ok — I can prototype a generator change that emits `.pyi` and also a small change to the streaming helpers to accept a `type_hint` param which, when provided, changes the returned async iterator type signature (only at annotation time). example patch idea:
```python
# runtime: unchanged
def stream_chat(..., type_hint: Optional[type] = None) -> AsyncIterator[Any]:
    # if type_hint is provided, it's only for static annotations
    ...
# pyi (emit):
def stream_chat(..., type_hint: Optional[Type[ChatDelta]] = ...) -> AsyncIterator[ChatDelta]: ...
```

jun: that looks like a good pattern. we'll need to update the docs and add a mypy config in sample-app to ignore the `--disallow-any` false positives until we roll out. also ensure `py.typed` is present in the package if we include inline types.

ci-bot: CI failure: pyright check failed in sample-app (branch: emma/pyi-stubs) — see https://ci.redwood.example/build/1123 :thinking:

maria: thanks, I'll pull the branch and run pyright locally. if pyi approach gets green for pyright and mypy, we can change the release checklist to include a types smoke test.

kai: one more gotcha — consumers who pin old Python (<3.9) might still get `list[]` vs `typing.List` mismatch. recommend we normalise emitted pyi to typing.List and include `from __future__ import annotations` header to be safe.

emma: thanks team — I'll open a draft PR with `--emit-pyi` flag and a small sample-app test that runs mypy/pyright in CI. cc: @jun for review when ready. :thumbsup:
